issues.legal_issue: A tribunal assigned authority over agricultural tenancy questions has exclusive jurisdiction to decide rival claims as to who held the tenancy, including whether the tenancy belonged to an individual or a joint family.
material_facts: A civil suit for injunction was based on an alleged tenancy, and the parties disputed whether the tenancy was held by the plaintiff individually or by the joint family.
The civil court referred the tenancy question to the tribunal, which found that the tenancy was in favour of the joint family.
The tribunal separately considered rival claims to registration, and the civil courts treated the tribunal's determination as controlling.
issues.conclusion: The tribunal alone had jurisdiction to decide the rival tenancy claims; the civil court could decide other issues in the suit but could not decide the tenancy question.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 48A(5), 112(B)(b) and (bbb), and 133 empower the tribunal to determine rival claims to registration and questions of tenancy, and make its decision final; Section 133 prevents a civil court from deciding the referred tenancy question, while allowing it to proceed on other matters. The statutory scheme impliedly excludes civil-court jurisdiction under Section 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The Court approved the view in Guruvappa v. Manjappu Hengsu and found it consistent with Noor Mohd. Khan Ghouse Khan Soudagar v. Fakirappa Bharmappa Machenaballi; it held Appi Belchadthi v. Sheshi Belchadthi not to be good law.

predicates.civil_suit_involves_tenancy_question: A civil suit concerning land includes a dispute about whether a person was its tenant.
predicates.tribunal_received_rival_tenancy_claims: Rival claims about the tenancy were presented to the tribunal empowered to decide tenancy matters.

issues.definition: When a civil suit includes a tenancy dispute and rival tenancy claims are before the empowered tribunal, the tribunal alone decides the tenancy question.

issues.legal_issue: Cultivation of land by any member of a joint family is treated as personal cultivation by the joint family for determining tenancy status.
material_facts: The dispute concerned whether the alleged tenancy belonged to an individual or to a joint family.
The case involved cultivation by a member of the family, and the family asserted a tenancy claim.
issues.conclusion: For the statutory tenancy inquiry, land cultivated by any member of a joint family is deemed to be cultivated personally by the joint family.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(11), Explanation II, provides that land is deemed to be cultivated personally by a joint family if cultivated by any member of that family; Section 2(17) defines a joint family. Read with Sections 45 and 48A, these provisions make the joint family the relevant cultivating tenant for the registration inquiry when a family member cultivates the land.

predicates.agricultural_tenancy_registration_disput: A proceeding concerns the determination of tenant status or registration as an occupant of agricultural land.
predicates.joint_family_member_cultivated_land: A member of a joint family cultivated the land.

issues.definition: In an agricultural tenancy-registration dispute, cultivation of the land by a joint-family member means that the joint family is treated as the personal cultivator.

issues.legal_issue: A tenancy determination that has been upheld in a concluded challenge and has become final bars reopening the same tenancy dispute in the civil appeal.
material_facts: The tribunal independently considered the rival tenancy claims and reached the same determination as in the earlier inquiry.
A challenge to the tribunal's determination was later disposed of upholding it, and that determination became final before the appeal was decided.
The appeal concerned the same underlying tenancy dispute.
issues.conclusion: The final tribunal determination operated as res judicata, providing an additional reason to dismiss the appeal without interference.
issues.legal_principle: A determination of the same tenancy dispute that has been upheld in a concluded challenge and has become final operates as res judicata; the Court relied on that finality as an independent ground for dismissing the appeal. No earlier case or statutory provision is cited for this ground.

predicates.appeal_from_civil_injunction_suit: An appeal arises from a civil suit seeking an injunction concerning land.
predicates.tribunal_decided_same_tenancy_dispute: The tribunal determined the tenancy dispute that is also raised in the appeal.
predicates.challenge_to_tribunal_decision_became_fi: A challenge to the tribunal's determination was concluded, upheld the determination, and became final.

issues.definition: When an appeal from a civil injunction suit raises a tenancy dispute already determined by the tribunal and the challenge to that determination has become final, the same dispute is barred by res judicata.
